checkpoint: 1 — the frame before, and the place in the draw order the defect lives at
note: PNGs land under .artifacts/evidence/156-* per Resolve-EvidenceOutputRoot and are not committed, per AGENTS.md's rule against committing large derived files. This file records the reproduction commands, the image hashes, the commit each capture was taken against — copied from the manifest capture-evidence.ps1 itself wrote (.artifacts/evidence/156-before/manifest.json), not retyped — and the measurement that says the same thing in numbers.
complaint: Owner, playtest 2026-08-01: «наверно существо должно быть над границей комнаты, а не под ней». On the frame the goblins on the bottom row of the kitchen and the larder each have their own room's outline drawn across them.

whereTheDefectLives.claim: Not in the border's coordinates. In which pass it is drawn in.

beforeThisIssue.reading: DrawElevatedWorld is the whole depth pass — walls, posts, creatures and raiders in Y-order. DrawRoomBorders runs after it, so every stroke of every room's outline is painted over every body standing on it.

whereTheDefectLives.whyTheRuleOfThatPassDidNotCatchIt: OverlayMark.RoomBorder is declared StrokeOnly in InformationalOverlays, and the reason recorded next to it was «the border is a line on the inside edge of the patch and never fills, so nothing standing in the room is hidden by it». Fill was never the point; covering was. A 2.0 reference-pixel stroke drawn across a 22 reference-pixel cell covers a body whether or not it fills.
whereTheDefectLives.whyItCannotSimplyMoveDown: A wall standing directly south of a room cell is drawn in front of that cell and covers the bottom of it outright. Clearing that would cost a base inset of 10.625 reference px against a MaximumBorderInset of 10.0, so no inset is an answer — see RoomWallClearanceTests.A_wall_in_front_of_a_room_cannot_be_cleared_by_any_inset and docs/engineering/PROTOTYPE_GRAYBOX.md. Moving the whole border below the depth pass therefore trades this defect for Issue #139's and #147's.

measurement.committedWith: checkpoint 2 — the test restates the pre-#156 arrangement (PreIssue156Layer: every segment above the depth pass) so this column stays reproducible after the arrangement is gone, the same way RoomWallClearanceTests.PreIssue147Inset does
measurement.method: For every room PresentationFixtures.Baseline(1) publishes, every segment RoomGeometry.BorderEdges draws, and every cell of the map a body can stand on — plus the midpoint of every orthogonal step between two such cells, because a render centre is interpolated — the border's stroke band (RoomGeometry.StrokeBand: the line widened by BorderStrokeHalfWidth, which is what Main draws) is intersected with the body's drawn rectangle (CameraView.GoblinDrawSize square, which is what Main.DrawGoblin draws the sprite into and is wider than the disc under it). An overlap counts as a crossing unless walls this frame draws in front of that body — rock tiles whose depth anchor is behind the body's — paint over the whole of it together, measured against WallRenderGeometry.DrawnBands.
measurement.pinning: 226 and the list of four rooms are asserted, not merely quoted: the test carries Assert.Equal(226, crossings.Count) and Assert.Equal on the room list at each of the three tile sizes. Independent review found the first version of it asserting only crossings.Count > 0, which left the headline number of the issue held up by prose — the pattern it was modelled on, RoomWallClearanceTests.The_pre_147_ladder…, pins its own figure with Assert.Equal([0.375], quarters).
